text: A decorator is just a function that wraps another function and changes what it does.
Shout takes a function called func and returns a brand new function built around it.
The inner wrapper accepts anything at all — star args and double-star kwargs catch every argument.
Inside, it calls the original function and keeps the result.
Then it upper-cases that result and adds an exclamation mark before handing it back.
Line five returns the wrapper itself, not a call to it — that distinction matters.
Now watch the at-sign syntax sitting right above greet.
At-shout quietly replaces greet with shout of greet — same name, new behaviour.
So calling greet with world doesn't politely say hello, it shouts it.
Same function, zero changes to its body.
